title: Which triangle shapes fold into a tetrahedron?
description: Four shapes made of equal triangles are folded in the mind, with three faces at every corner of a regular tetrahedron. The board finds the two nets. Keeko's doubt is that any four triangles will fold into a tetrahedron.
teaching_notes: One idea: a regular tetrahedron has four triangle faces and three meet at each corner, so a net must fold with exactly three faces at every corner. Watch for students who count the four triangles and stop there.

source: Four shapes are made of equilateral triangles: a large trian
video_script.why: The child decides which shapes are nets of a regular tetrahedron by folding in the mind, because a net needs three faces at every corner and four faces in all.
video_script.substitution: four shapes: a large triangle of four, four triangles round one point, a straight strip of four, and a strip of four with a fifth triangle below.
video_script.anchor: the four shapes of equal triangles from the book, folded one by one on the stage
video_script.wrong_answer: any four triangles joined edge to edge will fold into a tetrahedron
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says any four triangles will do because a tetrahedron has four faces; but four triangles round one point crowd four faces at one corner, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Only the large triangle and the straight strip of four are nets of a regular tetrahedron

final_answer.value: Only the large triangle and the straight strip of 4
final_answer.spoken: only the large triangle and the straight strip of four

hold_back: Only the large triangle and the straight strip of 4
maths_rules: a regular tetrahedron has 4 faces, all equal triangles, and 3 faces meet at each corner
large triangle of 4: the three corner triangles fold up round the middle one and meet at one point: a net
4 triangles round one point: 4 faces would meet at that corner, not 3: not a net
straight strip of 4: folds along the shared edges and closes into a tetrahedron: a net
strip of 4 with a fifth triangle: 5 triangles, one more than the 4 faces: not a net
video_script.design: One idea: count the faces at a corner. Each shape folds on the stage; the crowded corner and the extra triangle glow in the warning colour.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about four shapes.
<bookmark mark='shapes'/>Each shape is made of triangles with all three sides equal.
<bookmark mark='tetra'/>A regular tetrahedron means a solid with four equal triangle faces.
<bookmark mark='net'/>A net means a flat shape that folds into the solid.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of the four shapes are nets of a regular tetrahedron?

narration: <bookmark mark='faces'/>A regular tetrahedron has four faces, and each face is a triangle.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>Look at any one corner. Exactly three faces meet there.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>A net must fold with three faces at every corner.

narration: <bookmark mark='large'/>Step one, take the large triangle of four, and keep the middle triangle flat.
<bookmark mark='meet'/>Fold the three corner triangles up. They meet at one point with no gap, so it is a net.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: four triangles round one point: four faces would crowd one corner, not three; verdict: not a net

narration: <bookmark mark='fan'/>Step two, take the four triangles that all meet round one point.
<bookmark mark='crowd'/>Four faces would meet at that corner, but a tetrahedron has three. This is not a net.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the straight strip of 4 folds along the shared edges and closes into a tetrahedron; verdict: a net

narration: <bookmark mark='strip'/>Step three, take the straight strip of four triangles in one row.
<bookmark mark='close'/>Fold it along the edges between the triangles. It closes into a tetrahedron, so it is a net.

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step four, the strip with a fifth triangle below.
<bookmark mark='extra'/>It has five triangles, but the solid has only four faces. One is too many, so it is not a net.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Only the large triangle and the straight strip of four are nets of a regular tetrahedron.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks any four triangles joined edge to edge will fold into a tetrahedron.

<bookmark mark='fix'/>Four triangles are needed, but how they are joined decides if the shape closes.
